This is a Criminal Appeal filed under Section 374(3) of Cr.P.C. challenging the legality and correctness of the Judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the XII ACMM,
Bengaluru in C.C.No.11729/2016 dated:
17.11.2019.
The appellant is the accused and the respondent is the complainant before the Trial Court and the same rank would be referred to hereinafter for the sake of convenience.

2. The essential facts required for disposal of this appeal are as under:
That the respondent / complainant is the family friend of the accused and accused had approached complainant stating that he is in financial requirement to purchase agricultural land and for family necessity.
The 3 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 complainant had paid a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- in the month of January, 2015 by way of cash.
At the taking the said amount the accused had assured the complainant that said amount will be returned by him within a span of 6months i.e. on or before the end of June,2015.
Believing his words, the complainant had waited until the end of June,2015.

But,
in spite of specified period, the said Rajanna had chosen not to repay the amount of hand loan to the complainant.

Whenever the complainant used to seek the return of his amount, the said Rajanna had started to avoid him and after hectic search the Rajanna used to give one or the other evasive replies to the complainant.
The accused has issued cheque for Rs.10,00,000/- bearing No.522872 dated: 24.06.2015.

The complainant has presented said cheque to his Banker State Bank of Mysore,
Hanumantha Nagar Branch, Bengaluru, but said cheque was returned unpaid with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" on 01.07.2015.

The complainant had waited till 17.08.2015 and again the complainant has presented said cheque for 4 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 encashment on 02.08.2015, but it returned with an endorsement as "Funds Insufficient" on 21.08.2015.
Hence, the complainant got issued legal notice on 10.09.2015.
The legal notice is duly served on accused on 29.09.2015.
In spite of service of legal notice, the accused has not chosen to reply nor complied.

Hence, the complainant has complaint on 20.11.2015.
3.
The Trail Court issued process against the accused for the offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act.
The accused has appeared through his learned Counsel and pleaded not guilty.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the complainant is examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4.
After closure of evidence of complainant, statement of the accused as required under Section 313 of Cr.P.C is recorded.
The accused is examined as D.W.1.
The accused has not produced any documents.

After hearing the both sides, Trail Court considering the material on record convicted the accused for the offence under Section 138 of N.I Act and sentenced accused to pay a 5 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 fine of Rs.1,00,000/-.
The same shall be paid within a period of 30 days from the date of this order.
Further, Trial Court has directed to pay the compensation of Rs.98,000/- to the complainant out of fine amount.
In default of payment of fine amount, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for 1 month.

2. The impugned order by the Trail Court is highly erroneous and against the principles of natural justice.
3. That the Trial Court wrongly made an order without no evidence on record by the complainant and to the case in the complaint and order for conviction to the Accused/Appellant.

"the Ex.P.3 legal notice dated: 24.06.2015 an amount of Rs. 6,00,000/- pertaining to the cheque of Bank of Canara Bank Tumakuru belongs to accused person was written by the instructions on the complainant himself" and in further he also admits that:
"Complainant is a M.A. Graduate" and in further admits that: "the complainant was not produced the supported documents in separately in support of lend money to the accused" and in further admits that: "the complainant has the not produced the documents in support and to prove that Rajanna vs Srikanth H G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11227984/
3 8 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 and in amount of lending the same to the reference and source"
and in further admitted that: "the complainant was not produced IT returns in support of lending money" and in the cross examination of P.W.1 dated: 19.04.2017 at page No.4 admits that: "in the complaint has not mentioned the date and time of the money was lend to the accused particularly"
and in further "in the complaint or in chief or in notice, the complainant has not mentioned the place of asking for the amount of loan by the accused before the complainant" and in further the P.W.1 also admits that: "in chief or in notice or in complaint have not mentioned the detailed of date and witness to the presence at the place that the complainant was paid the amount to the accused."
8. The Trial Court was failed to observe the observations put-forth in the complaint or in chief or in the witness box or in the cross examination of P.W.1 which was elicited the truth by the accused against the complaint.

On basis of the facts and circumstances on record, the following Points are arises for my consideration:
POINTS 1.
Whether the appellant has made out grounds to condone delay of 51 days as sought in application filed U/Sec. 5 of Limitation Act?
12 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 2.

9. My findings on the above Points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Point No.2 : In the Negative.

Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. POINT NO.1:
The appellant has filed application U/Sec.5 of Limitation Act, seeking to condone the delay of 51 days in preferring this appeal.

Along with the application, the appellant has filed affidavit wherein it is stated that he could not challenge Judgment in time due to his ill health that he is suffering from decease of Chikkengunya and he was advised to take bed-rest for a period of 2 months and he was not contacted his Counsel.
The Medical certificate is produced by the appellant.
Hence,appellant prays to allow application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act.
13 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 11.
The respondent is remained absent in instant case.
12. As far as considering the question of condonation of delay is concerned, the question is no longer a res-Integra.

Now judicial trend is in favour of taking lenient view while considering the application Rajanna vs Srikanth H G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11227984/
5 for condonation of delay.

At this juncture, it is pertinent to place reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in AIR 1987 Supreme Court 1353 (Collector, Land Acquisition,
Anantnag and another -Vs- Mst. Katiji and Others), wherein the principles are succinctly laid down as under:
"The legislature has conferred the power to condone delay by enacting S. 5 of the Indian Limitation Act of 1963 in order to enable the courts to do substantial justice to parties by disposing of matters on 'merits'.

The expression "sufficient cause"
employed by the legislature is adequately elastic to enable the Courts to apply the law in a meaningful manner which subserves the ends of justice that being the 14 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 life-purpose for the existence of the institution of Courts.
It is common knowledge that this Court has been making a justifiably liberal approach in matters instituted in this Court.
But the message does not appear to have percolated down to all the other Courts in the hierarchy.

And such a liberal approach is adopted on principle as it is realised that:
1. Ordinarily a litigant does not stand to benefit by lodging an appeal late.
2. Refusing to condone delay can result in a meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold and cause of justice being defeated.
As against this when delay is  condoned the highest that can  happen is that a cause would be decided on merits after hearing the parties.
3."Even day's delay must be explained" does not mean that a pedantic approach should be made.
Why not every hour's delay, every second's delay?
The doctrine must 15 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 be applied in a rational common sense pragmatic manner.

4.When substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other, cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non-deliberate delay.
5. There is no presumptions that delay is occasioned deliberately, or on account of culpable negligence, or on account of malafides.
A litigant does not stand to benefit by resorting to delay.

In fact he runs a serious risk.
6.
It must be grasped that judiciary is respected not on account of its power to legalize injustice on technical grounds but because it is capable of removing injustice and is expected to do so."

Even that apart only on the ground of the delay, merit of the case cannot be thrown to overboard.
Hence, considering all these aspects of the case, medical documents filed and totality of the circumstances, I answer Point No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. POINT NO.2:
The complainant has filed complaint on 20.11.2015.
The process was issued to the accused on 05.05.2016.
The accused had appeared through his Counsel and he got bail on 08.07.2016.
His plea is recorded on 12.07.2016.
The complainant has filed an affidavit as examination-in-chief and he is examined as P.W.1.
The P.W.1 has reiterated the contents complainant.
The complainant has relied documentary evidence at Ex.P.1 to 4.
After closure of evidence of complainant, statement of the accused as required under 17 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 Section 313 of Cr.P.C is recorded.
The accused has filed an affidavit as examination-in-chief and he is examined as D.W.1.
The defence of the accused is one of total denial of case.
The accused has not produced any documents.

14. The complainant on oath has deposed as P.W.1 that for repayment of hand loan taken by him,
the accused has issued cheque for Rs.10,00,000/- bearing No.522872 dated: 24.06.2015 and the complainant has presented said cheque to his Banker State Bank of Mysore, Hanumantha Nagar Branch, Bengaluru, but said cheque was returned unpaid with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient"
on 01.07.2015 and the complainant had waited till 17.08.2015 and again the complainant has presented said cheque for encashment on 02.08.2015, but it returned with an endorsement as "Funds Insufficient" on 21.08.2015 and hence, the complainant got issued legal notice on 10.09.2015 and in spite of receipt of legal notice, the accused has not chosen to reply nor complied.
The P.W.1 has denied in cross 18 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 examination that, he had not paid loan amount of Rs.10,00,000/- to accused in his house.
The complainant has produced the cheque as per Ex.P.1.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 which shows that, accused has issued cheque bearing No.522872,
dated: 24.06.2015, drawn on Canara Bank, Main Branch, Tumkur for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/-in favour of complainant.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 which shows that, said cheque dishonored due to 'Funds Insufficient' on 21.08.2015.
The complainant has produced the legal notice as per Ex.P.3 dated: 10.09.2015.
On perusal of Ex.P.4 which shows that, the accused has received legal notice.
15. The accused has denied entire case of complainant.
The accused is examined as D.W.1.
The accused has not produced any documents in support of his contention.
16. The learned Counsel for Appellant has vehemently argued that the complaint is not maintainable.

The Counsel for appellant has relied upon decisions as under:
19 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 1. (2014) BC 3 (SC) in case of John K. Abraham -Vs- Simon C. Abraham and Another.
2. 2015(4) Kar.L.J.118 (SC) in case of K. Subramani -Vs- K. Damodara Naidu.

sentences.text: I have bestowed my anxious considerations to the principles emerges from these decisions.
17. The cheque has been drawn by the accused in favour of the complainant.
The cheque has got presumption under Section 139 of N.I. Act.
Such presumption has not been rebutted by the accused in accordance with law by leading corroborative evidence.
The cheque has been presented for encashment in time and even notice has been issued in accordance with law.
The complaint has been filed in time.
The complainant has fulfilled the ingredients of the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
The principles laid down in above decisions relied by the Counsel for appellant are not applicable under facts and 20 Criminal Appeal No.235/2020 circumstances of this case.
Hence, the complaint filed by the complainant is maintainable.
Therefore, I hold that the Trial Court has not committed any error either on facts or in law in convicting the accused.
Thus, the Judgment shall not be interfered with.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in the Negative.

ORDER
